- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., >50% negative values) and model forecasts are flat or rising, adjust downward by 2–5% to account for bearish sentiment bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If official event net supply is negative and model ignores it, add 1–3% downward bias to forecast, especially if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.  
- When sentiment is mixed (e.g., 0.33–0.67) and model is trending, apply mean reversion: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (e.g., first 5 days drop >5%), model often underestimates — increase initial forecast by 1–3% to compensate for lag.  
- If recent auction supply is CAP3 EU or DE and sentiment is bearish, reduce forecast by 1–2% per auction to reflect supply shock.  
- If sentiment is bullish but model is flat, add 0.5–1% upward bias to first 3 days to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
